We are excited to move forward on a web partnership, but we will need some adjustments before we can sign.\\nBelow are the key points we would like to revise.\\n*1- Scope of platforms: web only* \\nRight now, \\u201cLicensed Platforms\\u201d includes mobile app stores. Our intent for this deal is strictly web publishing and also excluding 2 web-platforms as described below.\\n\\u2022 Please limit Licensed Platforms to HTML5 / WebGL browser distribution only (for example <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and other web portals).\\n\\u2022 For the avoidance of doubt, the agreement should explicitly exclude any mobile app store or native mobile distribution. This method significantly increases the file size limit:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.\\n\\u2022 *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.\\n\\u2022 *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. *1- Scope of platforms: web only*

• Please limit Licensed Platforms to HTML5 / WebGL browser distribution only (for example <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and other web portals).

• We would like to also exclude YouTube playables and Telegram from the list. We’ll pursue those 2 web publishing paths on our own since we have good connections with the YouTube team directly and have an expert community builder on Telegram.

We are comfortable giving this a real shot, but the current structure creates a long lock-in with a long tail.
• Initial term: 12 months is fine, but we would like to add mutual termination for convenience after an initial test period. For example: after the first 3 months from launch, either party can terminate for convenience on 30 days written notice.

*3- Transferability and assignment*
We are not comfortable with a fully transferable license that can be assigned freely.
• The license should be non-transferable except to your wholly owned affiliates.
• Any assignment or transfer to a third party should require our prior written consent.
*4- Monetization and outbound links*
We understand that you control monetization on your portals, but we would appreciate some room to promote our own ecosystem. Is it possible to include links to the iOS and Android store pages for Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D? These links can follow your UX guidelines. This is not something we’ll pursue right away but we would like to reserve the options with your consent.

*5- SDK and post termination support*
We are fine integrating your SDK and keeping it up to date during the term, but not for an extended period after termination.
• Please remove the requirement to update or re-integrate the SDK for up to one year after termination.We are happy to commit to updating the SDK during the transition period.
• Post termination, we are happy to commit to keeping the last live version stable for a short transition period (for example 60 days), with critical bug fixes only and no new features or SDK migrations.
If you can accommodate these changes, we will be in a good position to move ahead quickly. Feel free to send a revised draft, or if it is easier, we can mark up the current one and return a redline.
Best regards,

Telegram games, which are built as Mini Apps, do not have a binary size restriction because they are web applications hosted on a developer’s server, not static files uploaded to Telegram’s servers. This is a key distinction from binary files like documents or videos that users upload. However, other file size limits apply to media that a Mini App or bot might send or receive.

File size restrictions for Telegram bots and Mini Apps
Standard Bot API
If your game uses the standard Telegram Bot API to send files (e.g., images, videos, or game assets), the following file size limits apply:

• *Photos:* 10 MB maximum.
• *Other files (including game assets):* 50 MB maximum. 
• 
Local Bot API server
For developers who need to exceed the standard limits, Telegram allows running a local Bot API server. This method significantly increases the file size limit:

• *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.
• *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.
• *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. Bots themselves cannot have a Premium account an[USERNAME_1352] therefore cannot upload files larger than 2000 MB. 
• 
Development and performance considerations
Game logic and assets
Since Mini Apps are web-based, the total size of your game is only limited by your hosting environment and browser performance. The following strategies are recommended for optimizing performance:

• *Server-side optimization:* Keep your game logic on your own server to minimize the data sent to the user.
• *Asset compression:* Compress and optimize images, videos, and other assets to reduce loading times. Tools like TinyPNG can help significantly.
• *Lazy loading:* Only load assets when they are needed, rather than all at once, to improve the initial loading speed.

Definitions
• Revenue: cash collected from Telegram users attributable to [PERSON_NAME_0133].
• Direct costs: UA on Telegram, creator payouts, refunds, chargebacks, payment processing, platform fees, promo credits, other variable costs.
• Net Profit: Revenue minus Direct costs, calculated monthly.
Tiered profit share, per month
• 20% on the first $25,000 of Net Profit
• 15% on the next $50,000 of Net Profit, i.e., $25,001 to $75,000
• 10% on Net Profit above $75,000
• Monthly cap: total payout to [PERSON_NAME_0133] cannot exceed $15,000 for that month
• Floor: if Net Profit is positive but under $5,000, pay the greater of calculated share or $500
• No payout if Net Profit ≤ 0
Why this structure
• Starts aggressive on the first dollars of profit, then steps down to 10%.
• The cap is reached at $100,000 monthly Net Profit:
    ◦ 20% of first $25,000 = $5,000
    ◦ 15% of next $50,000 = $7,500, cumulative $12,500
    ◦ 10% of next $25,000 = $2,500, cumulative $15,000 cap
Examples
1. Your scenario
• Revenue: 100,000 users × $0.50 = $50,000
• Direct costs: $10,000
• Net Profit: $40,000
• Payout: 20% of $25,000 = $5,000, plus 15% of $15,000 = $2,250, total $7,250
2. Strong month
• Net Profit: $100,000
• Uncapped math would be $16,250, but the monthly cap applies, payout = $15,000
3. Modest month
• Net Profit: $4,000
• Calculated share at 20% = $800, floor applies only if higher than share. Payout = $800
Attribution and scope
• Scope: Telegram only, assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] manages.
• Attribution: unique links or postbacks. Mixed traffic allocated by last touch on Telegram assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] controls.
• Refunds and chargebacks reduce Revenue in the period recognized.
Payment terms
• Close books on the 5th, pay by the 15th.
• Monthly report: Users, Revenue, Direct costs, Net Profit, tier math, and payout.

At the end of the automation flow in Helpshift, if the user does not log into the game for 7 days, their account will be deleted. If they log in during this period, the deletion process will be canceled.
I’ve prepared a document outlining the in-game flow, and <@EMPLOYEE_0012_SLACK_ID> has also prepared a flow for Helpshift
Could you please provide feedback on this flow? If the cost is too high, we’re open to making changes

Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.

content.text: No stale Telegram cards in Trello, and Helpshift Trello cards are all old/complete. The tracker "lie" is in Linear (master ENG-2377). **[Wind-down / tracker cleanup — Feb 28, 2026 · Arthur]** The Telegram DD initiative was **called off in early January 2026** and is not being pursued. On **Jan 6, 2026**, Leonard terminated our Telegram distribution contractor and confirmed we changed direction and "won't be doing telegram anytime soon."

Decision reference (Slack): https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C07C2866011/p1767727583081359

Action taken: closing this master ticket and all still-open Telegram sub-tickets as **Canceled** so the tracker reflects reality for the data handover. The groundwork that actually shipped stays marked **Done** as historical record: ENG-2378 (Update WebGL Branch), ENG-2379 (MiniApp Bot / DD integration), ENG-2387 (Jenkins Telegram builds). Everything else (payments, Telegram Stars pricing, referral, ads, crypto, friend leaderboards, faster loading, username hookup) was never built and is now Canceled.

content.text: Task 2 done. Now **Task 3 — Helpshift removal**: this has never been ticketed, so I'll create a tracked parent + two game-specific sub-tickets in Linear with the plan, deadline, decision link, and current status.

content.content: Updated task #2 status
Updated task #3 status

input.title: Remove Helpshift from Domino Delights & Zombie Match (wind-down)
input.description:
**Wind-down task — get both live games off Helpshift before the subscription lapses.**

Helpshift is being terminated as part of the company wind-down (Helpshift agreed to cancel our subscription). We must remove the Helpshift SDK / in-app support integration from both live games so the in-game "Contact Us" flow doesn't break once the account is gone.

**Plan (per Leonard, Feb 10, 2026):** replace the Helpshift-backed "Contact Us" support flow with a simple `mailto:` that opens the user's email app addressed to our player-support inbox. No data export needed — confirmed in the Helpshift termination notice ("We don't need to export any data").

**Deadline:** Feb 28–29, 2026 (Helpshift cutoff — the date we set with Leonard).

**Status as of Feb 28, 2026: NOT STARTED.** No removal branch or PR exists in either game repo yet (verified in GitHub — all Helpshift PRs to date are the original 2024–2025 integrations). This effort had been living in Slack and was untracked; creating this to track it.

**Decision / context (Slack #winddown):** https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C0ADGSZKR3R/p1770789534434749

Sub-tasks: Domino Delights (repo `GameOfDominoes`) and Zombie Match 3D (repo `match3d`).

📋 *Engineering wind-down rundown* (as of Feb 28) — cc <@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID>

*1. Tracker cleanup — Linear now reflects reality*
• *Telegram (DD):* the whole Telegram push was called off in early January (Leonard terminated the contractor on Jan 6, "changed directions, won't be doing telegram"). The tracker still showed it live. I closed the master ticket *ENG-2377* and all open sub-tickets as *Canceled*, with a note on the master linking the Jan decision so nobody has to dig for it. The 3 pieces that actually shipped (WebGL branch, MiniApp bot, Jenkins builds) stay Done for the record.
• *UI Optimization sprint:* a bunch were stuck in PR/Validation even though the code merged back in Nov. I checked GitHub and flipped the *11 that actually merged* to Done (Shop, Settings, Level-win, Level-lose, Nathan's Treasure, Axe Arena + all 4 Mini-Games). *9 turned out to have no code behind them at all* — never built despite their status: Leaderboard, Quest, Collect&Win, River Rush, Season Pass, Remove-Ad, Offers, Rate-us, Daily Gift. Noted on each; they won't be completed.

*2. Helpshift removal — DUE TODAY, and NOT started* ⚠️
This was living in chat and never ticketed. I've now tracked it: *ENG-2438* (parent) + *ENG-2441* (Domino Delights) + *ENG-2442* (Zombie Match). Plan per Leonard's Feb 10 note: rip out the Helpshift SDK in both games and repoint the in-game "Contact Us" button to a `mailto:` to our support inbox. No code exists in either repo yet — this is real work (SDK removal → build → store submission) and won't be in players' hands by tonight. Risk to flag: once Helpshift is cut off, the current Contact Us button breaks, so we either ship the mailto swap or accept a dead support button on live builds.

*3. Sunset handover — what they're still waiting on (my side)*
• *Linear + Trello exports into their shared drive* — the trackers are now cleaned up and accurate, so they're ready to export; dropping the files is the remaining step.
• *The Business+ question:* exporting *private* channels/DMs is not available on our current plan — Slack only exports public channels on Free/Pro. To hand over the private wind-down channels we'd need to upgrade to *Business+* (or Enterprise Grid) for a self-serve export, or file a Slack-approved compliance export request. Short answer for their tech guy: yes, private-channel export requires the Business+ upgrade.

*4. CrazyGames (web)*
We signed the web publishing agreement in early December (web-only: CrazyGames → MSN → Facebook → WeChat; Telegram + YouTube excluded) and *never started the integration* — no branch, no ticket, zero eng work. Their PM keeps pinging Robert. Given the wind-down we should just tell them plainly we won't be delivering it — needs a call from you two on how to close it out cleanly.

*5. Other genuinely-open eng items (moot in wind-down)*
A few stale DD tickets are still open under my name but won't be completed: ENG-2345 (addressables/storage), ENG-2396 (forced-ads kill switch), ENG-2363 (sign-in splash bug), ENG-2023 (bomb VFX). Not blockers — flagging so they're no surprise in the export.

*Net:* trackers are honest now. The one live-deadline item is *Helpshift removal today, not started* — need a call on whether we do the mailto swap today or let the support button go dark.
